topic: Hot take: the IMF warns of an AI market correction, and your AI skills still matter
post:
The IMF just warned that an AI market correction could shake the global financial system. 📉
My hot take: your AI skills are not in a bubble.

In its new Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF named an AI-driven correction as one of three near-term risks, alongside rising bond yields and cyber threats.

What it said 👇
⚠️ A correction could come if AI investment or profits disappoint
💸 It also notes growing evidence that AI capabilities can be delivered with less investment
🌍 In its scenario, unwinding AI investment cuts global GDP by up to 0.4% by 2028

Here's my take:
The IMF is talking about stock prices and spending. That's a different question from "is AI useful at work?"

The dot-com crash wiped out companies. It didn't wipe out the internet, or the people who learned to use it.

Why it matters:
If AI is getting cheaper to deliver, that's bad news for some investors and good news for everyone who uses it.

Practical takeaway:
Don't tie your learning to the headlines. Pick one AI tool, use it on real work every week, and keep a list of what it saves you. 📝

Do you think we're in an AI bubble? 👇
